questions.stem: Methanol (CH₃OH), ethanol (C₂H₅OH), and propan-1-ol (C₃H₇OH) have boiling points of 65°C, 78°C, and 97°C respectively. What causes this trend?

options.text: Longer chains have weaker O-H bonds that break more easily
Longer chains have stronger intermolecular forces due to more electrons and greater surface area
Shorter chains have more hydrogen bonds between molecules
Longer chains are more soluble in water, requiring more energy to boil

questions.explanation: As the carbon chain length increases, there are more electrons and a greater surface area for London dispersion forces between molecules. Although all alcohols also have hydrogen bonding (due to the -OH group), the increasing London forces with chain length explain the gradual rise in boiling point. Boiling breaks intermolecular forces, not the O-H bonds within molecules.

questions.stem: Ethanol dissolves completely in water, but hexan-1-ol barely dissolves. Both contain an -OH group. Why does solubility decrease with increasing chain length?

options.text: Longer alcohols have a weaker -OH group
The non-polar hydrocarbon chain dominates in longer alcohols, reducing their ability to form hydrogen bonds with water
Longer alcohols react with water instead of dissolving
Longer alcohols are solids and cannot dissolve

questions.explanation: The -OH group is the polar, hydrophilic (water-loving) part that can hydrogen bond with water. The hydrocarbon chain is non-polar and hydrophobic (water-repelling). In short alcohols like ethanol, the -OH group dominates and the molecule dissolves well. In longer alcohols, the large hydrophobic chain outweighs the -OH group's effect, making the molecule less soluble.

questions.stem: Ethanol is produced commercially by two methods: fermentation of sugars and hydration of ethene. Which statement correctly compares these methods?

options.text: Fermentation is faster and produces purer ethanol
Hydration of ethene is a continuous process using a catalyst, while fermentation is a batch process using enzymes at lower temperatures
Both methods use the same conditions and produce identical yields
Fermentation requires crude oil as a raw material

questions.explanation: Hydration of ethene (from crude oil) uses a phosphoric acid catalyst at high temperature (300°C) and pressure in a continuous process, producing relatively pure ethanol. Fermentation uses yeast enzymes at about 30-40°C in a batch process, producing a dilute solution that requires distillation. Fermentation uses renewable sugar crops, while hydration uses non-renewable crude oil.

questions.stem: The functional group of alcohols is -OH. A student says this means alcohols are alkalis because they contain hydroxide (OH⁻). Why is this incorrect?

options.text: The student is correct — all alcohols are alkaline
The -OH in alcohols is covalently bonded to carbon and does not dissociate into OH⁻ ions in solution; alcohols are neutral
Alcohols are actually acidic, not alkaline
The -OH group in alcohols is ionic

questions.explanation: In alkalis like NaOH, the OH⁻ is an ion that dissociates freely in water, making the solution alkaline. In alcohols, the -OH group is covalently bonded to a carbon atom and does not release OH⁻ ions into solution. Ethanol dissolved in water has a pH of approximately 7 (neutral). The same atoms (-OH) behave very differently depending on the type of bonding.

questions.stem: Ethanol is used as a fuel in some countries, often blended with petrol. When ethanol undergoes complete combustion, what are the products?

options.text: Carbon and water only
Carbon monoxide and hydrogen
Carbon dioxide and water
Ethanoic acid and water

questions.explanation: Complete combustion of ethanol produces carbon dioxide and water: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O. Ethanol is considered a greener fuel because it can be produced from renewable sugar crops (via fermentation), and the CO₂ released during combustion was absorbed by the plants during growth, making it closer to carbon-neutral than fossil fuels.
